title: The Cave That Giggled Back
synopsis: A goat discovers her own words coming back from a stone wall and ends by noticing smaller sounds.

related_resources.reason: Rebecca Parlakian, NAEYC (2020), point out changes and follow children’s curiosity; the cave scenario was not studied.
CDC (2026), More Parenting Tips and Activities: simple songs, rhymes and shared conversation; no claim of benefit from this narrative.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: A moment later, something answered from the cave.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: The delayed sound creates a small, nonthreatening listening question.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: These are caregiver/education practice sources relevant to the narrative approach; they did not study this story or establish a causal effect.

rationale_citations.story_anchor:
Fran listened carefully.

She could hear the word, just barely.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: An attention shift from loud to quiet is an authorial choice connected to supported noticing practices, not a validated intervention.
